cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a classic Kente cloth with hand-woven strip construction and the characteristic diamond/checkerboard weft-float patterning in yellow, green, red and black — a textile form strongly associated with the Ashanti (Akan) people of Ghana.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man’s wrapper composed of 23 hand-woven narrow strips entirely of rayon, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed to form a chequerboard pattern in the central part of the cloth; both ends have a variant design running continuously across the cloth that serves as a border to the main field. All the strips have the same base design with a warp of bands of varying width of green and yellow rayon. A chequerboard pattern is created in the main field of the cloth, consisting of diamonds in black, yellow and green, alternating with a pattern formed from elongated triangular shapes in the same colours. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
